questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of 1-(4-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl)propan-1-ol with activated $\text{MnO}_2$ in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ at room temperature selectively oxidizes which alcohol group(s)?
optionsEn: Only the primary benzylic alcohol to give 4-(1-hydroxypropyl)benzaldehyde
Only the secondary benzylic alcohol to give 1-(4-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl)propan-1-one
Both benzylic alcohol groups to give 4-propionylbenzaldehyde
Neither alcohol group, as $\text{MnO}_2$ oxidizes only allylic alcohols
questions.explanationEn: Activated $\text{MnO}_2$ is a chemoselective oxidant for both allylic and benzylic alcohols (primary or secondary), while leaving isolated saturated aliphatic alcohols untouched. Since both the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $-\text{CH(OH)Et}$ groups in 1-(4-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl)propan-1-ol are benzylic, excess activated $\text{MnO}_2$ oxidizes both to give 4-propionylbenzaldehyde.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Reduction of methyl 4-oxopentanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Me}$) with $1.0\text{ equiv}$ of $\text{NaBH}_4$ in $\text{MeOH}$ at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ affords predominantly:
questions.explanationEn: $\text{NaBH}_4$ is a mild, chemoselective hydride reducing agent that rapidly reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ while leaving ester groups completely untouched. Thus, the ketone at C4 is selectively reduced to give methyl 4-hydroxypentanoate (which may lactonize upon heating/acid, not immediately at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride ($\text{CyCOCl}$) with lithium dimethylcuprate ($\text{Me}_2\text{CuLi}$) in $\text{Et}_2\text{O}$ at $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ yields predominantly:
questions.explanationEn: Gilman reagents ($\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$) are soft, chemoselective organometallic nucleophiles that react rapidly with acid chlorides at $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ to form ketones and do NOT add further to the ketone product (unlike Grignard or organolithium reagents, which give tertiary alcohols). Thus, $\text{CyCOCl} + \text{Me}_2\text{CuLi}$ cleanly gives 1-cyclohexylethan-1-one.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Thermal electrocyclic ring closure of $(2E,4Z,6E)$-octa-2,4,6-triene proceeds in a:
questions.explanationEn: Hexatriene-to-cyclohexadiene cyclization is a $6\pi$-electron ($4n+2$, $n=1$) electrocyclic process, which is **disrotatory** under thermal conditions. In $(2E,4Z,6E)$-octa-2,4,6-triene, both terminal methyl groups point outward; disrotatory closure rotates both outward methyl groups to the same face of the ring, yielding *cis*-5,6-dimethylcyclohexa-1,3-diene.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Heating allyl phenyl ether ($\text{PhOCH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) at $200\,^\circ\text{C}$ yields 2-allylphenol via a:
optionsEn: Concerted $[3,3]$-sigmatropic Claisen rearrangement followed by tautomerization (rearomatization)
questions.explanationEn: Allyl phenyl ether undergoes a concerted thermal $[3,3]$-sigmatropic **Claisen rearrangement** to form 6-allylcyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one, which rapidly tautomerizes (keto-to-enol rearomatization) to yield 2-allylphenol.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following reagents selectively oxidize a primary alcohol ($\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$) to an aldehyde ($\text{RCHO}$) without over-oxidation to a carboxylic acid?
questions.explanationEn: PCC in anhydrous $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ (A), Dess-Martin periodinane (B), and Swern oxidation (D) operate under anhydrous/non-aqueous conditions so the intermediate aldehyde cannot form a hydrate, cleanly stopping at the aldehyde. Jones reagent (C) contains aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, which hydrates the aldehyde to a gem-diol and rapidly over-oxidizes it to the carboxylic acid. Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions typically retain the $(E)/(Z)$ double-bond geometry of an alkenyl coupling partner?
optionsEn: Suzuki-Miyaura coupling of an $(E)$-alkenylboronic acid with an aryl bromide
Stille coupling of a $(Z)$-alkenylstannane with an aryl triflate
Negishi coupling of an $(E)$-alkenylzinc halide with an aryl iodide
Radical Kolbe electrolysis of a carboxylic acid
questions.explanationEn: Suzuki-Miyaura (A), Stille (B), and Negishi (C) couplings proceed via oxidative addition, stereoretentive transmetalation, and stereoretentive reductive elimination at $\text{Pd}$, preserving the $(E)$ or $(Z)$ geometry of the alkenyl partner with high fidelity. Kolbe electrolysis (D) is a free-radical decarboxylative dimerization, not a Pd cross-coupling. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about photochemical reactions of carbonyl compounds are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In the Norrish Type II reaction, the intermediate 1,4-diradical can undergo either $\beta$-cleavage (fragmentation) or ring closure to a cyclobutanol (Yang cyclization)
Norrish Type I $\alpha$-cleavage of an unsymmetrical acyclic ketone selectively breaks the $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond that forms the MORE stable alkyl radical
Oxa-di-$\pi$-methane rearrangement of $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated ketones typically proceeds via a triplet ($T_1$) excited state to give a cyclopropyl ketone
All Paterno-Büchi reactions occur exclusively from the ground electronic state ($S_0$)
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: The Norrish Type II 1,4-diradical partitions between fragmentation (alkene + enol) and Yang cyclization (cyclobutanol). (B) True: $\alpha$-Cleavage preferentially cleaves the weaker $\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{C}$ bond leading to the more substituted/stabilized alkyl radical. (C) True: Triplet-sensitized irradiation of $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated ketones triggers the oxa-di-$\pi$-methane rearrangement to cyclopropyl ketones. (D) False: Paterno-Büchi is a photochemical $[2+2]$ cycloaddition requiring an electronically excited carbonyl ($S_1$ or $T_1$). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of moles of periodic acid ($\text{HIO}_4$) consumed per mole of hexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexol (D-glucitol) upon complete oxidative cleavage is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Periodic acid ($\text{HIO}_4$) cleaves every vicinal diol $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond in a $1:1$ molar stoichiometry. Hexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexol has $6$ contiguous hydroxyl-bearing carbons linked by $5$ vicinal $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds (C1–C2, C2–C3, C3–C4, C4–C5, and C5–C6). Complete oxidative cleavage therefore consumes exactly $5\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HIO}_4$ (yielding $2\text{ mol }\text{HCHO}$ and $4\text{ mol }\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Assuming all four $\text{Al}-\text{H}$ bonds of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ are utilized as hydride donors, the minimum number of moles of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ required to completely reduce $2.0\text{ mol}$ of trimethyl benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylate into benzene-1,3,5-triyltrimethanol is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Reduction of each ester group ($-\text{CO}_2\text{Me} \to -\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) requires $2$ equivalents of hydride ($\text{H}^-$). Each molecule of trimethyl benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylate contains $3$ ester groups, requiring $3 \times 2 = 6$ hydrides per mole. For $2.0\text{ mol}$ of triester, $12\text{ mol}$ of hydride are needed. Since $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ supplies $4\text{ mol}$ of hydride, the minimum amount required is $12 / 4 = 3\text{ mol}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation of $(E)$-hex-2-en-1-ol (drawn in the standard orientation with the allylic $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group at the **lower-right** and the propyl chain at the upper-left) using $\text{Ti(O}i\text{-Pr)}_4$, $t\text{-BuOOH}$, and **$(+)$-diethyl tartrate ($\text{L-(+)-DET}$)**, oxygen delivery occurs selectively from the:
questions.explanationEn: By the Sharpless mnemonic, when an allylic alcohol is drawn with the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group at the **lower-right**, $\text{L-(+)-DET}$ (natural tartrate) delivers oxygen selectively from the **bottom face** (whereas $\text{D-(-)-DET}$ delivers from the top face). Epoxidation of $(E)$-hex-2-en-1-ol from the bottom face yields $(2S,3S)$-2,3-epoxyhexan-1-ol.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The major product formed when 2-methylcyclohexan-1-one is subjected to the **Shapiro reaction** (1. $\text{TsNHNH}_2$, cat. $\text{H}^+$; 2. $n\text{-BuLi}$ ($2.2\text{ equiv}$), THF, $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ to $0\,^\circ\text{C}$; 3. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is:
questions.explanationEn: In the Shapiro reaction of an unsymmetrical ketone tosylhydrazone with $2\text{ equiv}$ of alkyllithium ($n\text{-BuLi}$), the first equivalent deprotonates the $\text{N}-\text{H}$ proton and the second equivalent selectively deprotonates the **less sterically hindered $\alpha$-carbon** (C6 rather than C2) syn to the sulfonyl group. Loss of $\text{Ts}^-$ and $\text{N}_2$ generates the less substituted vinyllithium (6-methylcyclohex-1-en-1-yllithium), which upon protonation with $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ yields **3-methylcyclohex-1-ene**.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the **Buchwald-Hartwig amination**, coupling of 4-bromotoluene with morpholine to form 4-($p$-tolyl)morpholine requires which catalytic system?
optionsEn: $\text{Pd}_2(\text{dba})_3$, a bulky phosphine ligand (e.g., BINAP or XPhos), and $\text{NaO}t\text{-Bu}$
questions.explanationEn: Buchwald-Hartwig $\text{C}-\text{N}$ cross-coupling uses a $\text{Pd}(0)$ precatalyst (such as $\text{Pd}_2(\text{dba})_3$), a bulky electron-rich phosphine ligand (e.g., BINAP, XPhos, or $\text{P}(t\text{-Bu})_3$) to promote oxidative addition and reductive elimination, and a stoichiometric strong base (commonly $\text{NaO}t\text{-Bu}$ or $\text{Cs}_2\text{CO}_3$) to deprotonate the Pd-coordinated amine.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the thermal conrotatory ring opening of *3-formylcyclobut-1-ene* (or 3-methoxycyclobut-1-ene), **torquoselectivity** predicts that an electron-donating substituent ($-\text{OMe}$) rotates predominantly:
optionsEn: Outward to give $(E)$-1-methoxybuta-1,3-diene, whereas a strong $\pi$-acceptor ($-\text{CHO}$) rotates inward to give $(Z)$-penta-2,4-dienal
Inward to give $(Z)$-1-methoxybuta-1,3-diene, whereas $-\text{CHO}$ rotates outward
Outward for both $-\text{OMe}$ and $-\text{CHO}$ purely due to sterics
questions.explanationEn: Houk's torquoselectivity principle shows that during conrotatory cyclobutene ring opening, $\pi$-electron-donating substituents ($-\text{OMe}$, $-\text{OR}$, $-\text{F}$) prefer **outward** rotation to avoid destabilizing filled–filled overlap with the breaking $\sigma$-bond (giving the $(E)$-diene), whereas strong $\pi$-electron-acceptors with a low-lying empty orbital ($-\text{CHO}$, $-\text{BH}_2$) prefer **inward** rotation for stabilizing donor–acceptor $\sigma \to \pi^*$ overlap (giving the $(Z)$-diene).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the **Ireland-Claisen rearrangement**, treatment of allyl propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) with $\text{LDA}$ and $\text{TMSCl}$ in THF (forming the $(E)$-silyl ketene acetal) followed by warming to $65\,^\circ\text{C}$ and aqueous workup gives:
questions.explanationEn: Deprotonation of allyl propanoate with $\text{LDA}$ and $O$-silylation with $\text{TMSCl}$ generates the allyl silyl ketene acetal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C(OTMS)OCH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. Upon gentle warming ($\sim 65\,^\circ\text{C}$), this 1,5-diene undergoes a facile $[3,3]$-sigmatropic Claisen rearrangement to form the trimethylsilyl ester of **2-methylpent-4-enoic acid**, which hydrolyzes upon workup to the free carboxylic acid.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about **Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation** (using AD-mix-$\alpha$ or AD-mix-$\beta$) are CORRECT?
optionsEn: AD-mix-$\alpha$ contains the chiral ligand $(\text{DHQ})_2\text{PHAL}$ and delivers the two $-\text{OH}$ groups from the bottom ($\alpha$) face when the alkene is oriented according to the Sharpless mnemonic
AD-mix-$\beta$ contains the pseudoenantiomeric ligand $(\text{DHQD})_2\text{PHAL}$ and delivers the two $-\text{OH}$ groups from the top ($\beta$) face
$\text{K}_3\text{Fe(CN)}_6$ acts as the stoichiometric co-oxidant that reoxidizes $\text{Os(VI)}$ back to $\text{Os(VIII)}$
It proceeds via *anti*-dihydroxylation of the alkene
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: AD-mix-$\alpha$ uses $(\text{DHQ})_2\text{PHAL}$ for bottom-face ($\alpha$) attack. (B) True: AD-mix-$\beta$ uses $(\text{DHQD})_2\text{PHAL}$ for top-face ($\beta$) attack. (C) True: $\text{K}_3\text{Fe(CN)}_6$ in the biphasic $t\text{-BuOH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ system reoxidizes $\text{Os(VI)}$ to $\text{OsO}_4$ ($\text{Os(VIII)}$) while $\text{MeSO}_2\text{NH}_2$ accelerates osmate ester hydrolysis. (D) False: $\text{OsO}_4$ dihydroxylation is strictly a concerted ***syn***-dihydroxylation. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following electrocyclic reactions proceed via a **disrotatory** pathway?
optionsEn: Thermal ring closure of the pentadienyl cation ($4\pi$, Nazarov cyclization)
questions.explanationEn: By the Woodward-Hoffmann rules, **disrotatory** motion is allowed for $(4n+2)\pi$ thermal reactions and $4n\pi$ photochemical reactions. Thus, thermal $6\pi$ triene closure (A), photochemical $4\pi$ cyclobutene opening (B), and photochemical $4\pi$ diene closure (D) are all disrotatory. The thermal Nazarov cyclization (C) is a $4\pi$ thermal electrocyclization and is strictly **conrotatory**. Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the **Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag (HLF)** reaction are CORRECT?
optionsEn: It converts an $N$-haloamine (typically $N$-chloroamine) into a 5-membered pyrrolidine ring upon photolysis ($h\nu$) or heating in strong acid followed by basification
The key step is intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen atom abstraction ($\delta$-H abstraction) by an aminium radical cation ($\text{R}_2\text{N}^+\text{H}^{\bullet}$)
The final ring closure occurs via intramolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ displacement of halide from the $\delta$-haloamine intermediate upon treatment with base
It selectively forms a 3-membered aziridine ring via $\alpha$-hydrogen abstraction
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: The HLF reaction synthesizes pyrrolidines from $N$-haloamines bearing a $\delta$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond. (B) True: Protonation and homolysis generate an aminium radical cation that abstracts the $\delta$-H via a 6-membered chair-like TS (1,5-HAT). (C) True: Chain transfer gives a $\delta$-haloamine, which cyclizes via intramolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ upon basification. (D) False: It forms 5-membered pyrrolidines, not aziridines. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: 2,2-Diallylcyclohexan-1-one ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{18}\text{O}$) is treated with Grubbs' second-generation ruthenium catalyst ($2\text{ mol}\%$) in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ at reflux to undergo ring-closing metathesis (RCM). The total number of carbon atoms present in the resulting spirocyclic ketone product is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: 2,2-Diallylcyclohexan-1-one has $6$ ring carbons plus $2 \times 3 = 6$ carbons in the two allyl ($-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) chains, totaling $12$ carbons. Intramolecular ring-closing metathesis between the two terminal alkenes eliminates $1\text{ equiv}$ of ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, $2$ carbons) to form spiro[4.5]dec-2-en-6-one ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{14}\text{O}$), which contains $12 - 2 = 10$ carbon atoms.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers (including both *endo* and *exo* diastereomers and all enantiomers) theoretically possible from the concerted $[4+2]$ Diels-Alder reaction of $(E)$-1-phenylbuta-1,3-diene with maleic anhydride is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The concerted $[4+2]$ cycloaddition of $(E)$-1-phenylbuta-1,3-diene with maleic anhydride creates $3$ stereocenters, but the two succinic anhydride carbons must remain *cis* (suprafacial addition). Thus, only two diastereomeric adducts can form: the *endo* adduct (phenyl *cis* to the anhydride bridge) and the *exo* adduct (phenyl *trans* to the anhydride bridge). Because both reactants are achiral and both adducts lack any symmetry plane ($C_1$), each diastereomer forms as a racemic pair of $2$ enantiomers, giving $2 + 2 = 4$ stereoisomers in total.
